mark: #1016's chained Q-B bench against 1107's actual configuration (tile-contiguous weights, threads=64 at (4096, 1280) block_M=64), CUDA-graph replay: gain where it claims, slower than 1107 in no M cell in any L2 state the bench measures (warm, cold, NEXT), bit-exact
patch_applies: in place of candidate-47's 0768 on the 1107 tree: 0762..0767, this 0768, 0769 all pass git apply --check and apply (setup_r1.sh, setup-r1.log); it changes only gemm.py and test_deepseek_v41_tilelang_linear.py, which no other patch touches
change: 1107's DECODE_FP8_CONFIGS plus one row change from #1016: the 64-row Q-B tiles of (12288, 1280) and (8192, 1280) go from block_N=64 (8192: num_stages=3) to block_N=128, block_K=128, num_stages=2. Everything else stays 1107's: the 16- and 32-row tiles, (4096, 1280) with threads=64 at block_M=64, and TILE_CONTIGUOUS_FP8 (no 16384/6144/2048 entries). The test asserts the 64-row tile of N >= 8192 is 128 x 128.
claim: TP3/TP4/TP5 Q-B decode at 33..64 rows with the weights warm in L2. On the chained bench pair: TP4 -3.1 us paired (consistent in all four processes, x-img -2.9 us) and TP3 -5.1 us paired (three of four processes; x-img -7.7 us, beyond TP3's 5.2 us warm A/A floor). With the indexer kernel as the model builds it: TP4 -3.0 us (beyond the interval) and TP3 -3.9 us (within the across-process interval). Cold and NEXT: no change within the interval. M = 1..24: the same kernels as 1107.
host: sp4 (spark-0012), NVIDIA GB10, driver 580.178.04; docker ps empty and ~/spark-hold.json absent before every run (recorded inside /tmp/spark-lab-gpu.lock in commands.txt)

arms.no1016: the image + candidate-47's 26 files with 0762..0767 and 0769 (no #1016), read-only; gemm.py is 1107's (546dbbcc1812)
arms.r1: the image + the same 26 files with 0762..0767, this 0768, 0769; gemm.py 3a7ecb3a49f6

method: One session on sp4. The ABBA order is no1016 boot1, r1 boot1, r1 boot2, no1016 boot2 (each a fresh container; h1016r1.py MODE=mark), followed by the pytest suite on r1 for two boots. A screening run (MODE=screen, no1016 overlay) came before the ABBA and chose the change. Each process times several config tables on the same weights, interleaved window by window in alternating order: 1107's real table, #1016 as submitted, r1, 1107 plus only the threads=64 drop, and the image's fp8_decode_config. Identical kernels are timed once per window. Each (pair, M) block takes 40 windows by CUDA-graph replay: warm (20 back-to-back pairs in one graph), cold (48 MiB flush, then one replay) and NEXT (flush, the NEXT-window L2 prefetch of the pair's weights and scales, join, then one replay). Before each block the GPU runs 100 ms or more of that block's own graph. Pairs: mark_tp4/mark_tp3 are the own-mark pair (h1016's), whose indexer kernel is built from the (4096, 1280) decode tiles as the PR bench builds it. prod_tp4/prod_tp3 are the same Q-B with the indexer kernel built exactly as linear.py builds decode_rope_mxfp4. qb_tp8 is the TP8 Q-B plain decode, the model's only other user of the (4096, 1280) tiles. The PDL LayerChain (production builders, Q-B 8192) runs at c1/c8/c8x6.
outcome_rule: same-kernels where r1 compiles 1107's kernels. Otherwise, gain or slower when the paired r1-1107 delta pooled over the four processes lies beyond the larger of its within-process CI95 and its across-process CI95 (t, 3 df), and the cross-image delta has the same sign. 'gain (x-img boot range; one process paired off)' when the within-process CI and separated cross-image boot ranges agree but one process does not. Otherwise within.

warm.outcome: gain (x-img boot range; one process paired off)

cold.outcome: gain (x-img boot range; one process paired off)

aa_note: At M = 1..24, r1's kernels are 1107's, so their cross-image deltas are an A/A floor between processes. That floor is up to 1.0 us warm at TP4 and up to 5.2 us warm / 4.8 us cold at TP3. TP3's chained warm working set (about 20 MiB) nearly fills L2, so its warm time depends on each process's allocation. Several same-kernels cells read 'slower' or 'gain' on the boot range and are noise.
layer_chain_note: Within the interval. c1 and c8 run the same kernels in both images, so their +13 / -24 us deltas are the chain's cross-process A/A spread. c8x6 (the only changed rows) is +14 +/- 36 us warm and +2 +/- 42 us cold. Digests are equal across images.
m12_cause: The bench (and h1016) builds the indexer's fused RoPE + MXFP4 kernel from fp8_decode_config(4096, 1280, block_M), whose threads default is 128. The epilogue covers the block_M x block_N tile in serial passes of 2 * threads / block_N rows: one thread per column pair, 16-lane shuffles for amax, predicated on m < M. Each pass carries dependent loads (Positions[m], then that row's CosSin) and the Q/S stores. #1016 raised block_N at block_M=16 from 64 to 128, which halves the rows per pass from 4 to 2. Live passes go from ceil(M/4) to ceil(M/2): equal at M = 1..2, 2 vs 1 at M = 3, 3 vs 2 at M = 6, 6 vs 3 at M = 12, 8 vs 4 at M = 16. The halved grid (32 CTAs instead of 64) saves about 1.3 us warm at M = 1, but every extra pass costs latency, so M = 12 comes out slower in every L2 state. The screen's diag isolates this on the indexer kernel alone at block_M=16, warm/cold medians in us: bN64/t128 6.59/36.94, bN128/t128 7.94/38.86, bN128/t256 (4 rows per pass again) 6.79/37.70. At M = 16 the gap is +1.7 warm and +3.4 cold. The model's own indexer kernel (bN128/t256/2 stages, never read from DECODE_FP8_CONFIGS) does not change with #1016. On the TP8 Q-B plain kernel, which has no serial epilogue, the 16-row block_N=128 tile has a smaller crossover: -1.7 us at M = 1, +0.4 us warm at M = 12 in every process. Its mechanism was not isolated.
findings: In the model, DECODE_FP8_CONFIGS[(4096, 1280)] reaches TP8's Q-B only. The indexer Q-B decode kernel (linear.py, decode_rope_mxfp4) is built with the kernel defaults (block_M 16, block_N 128, block_K 128, 2 stages, 256 threads) at every M, in 1107 and with #1016 alike. The chained bench's indexer half, built from the (4096, 1280) decode tiles, is therefore not what serving runs. In this harness the model's pair is faster than the bench's 1107 pair (TP4 M=48: 36.4 vs 45.3 us warm).

#1016's M=48 gain in cold and NEXT L2 came almost entirely from dropping threads=64 on (4096, 1280) at block_M=64. On the bench's indexer kernel that is -4.1 warm / -8.1 cold / -7.8 NEXT us (TP4, pooled), but the model never runs that kernel. On the model's consumer, TP8 Q-B, the same drop gains nothing: +0.23 warm, +1.20 cold, +1.45 NEXT us pooled over four processes (+0.20 / +0.54 / +0.37 in the screen). It is slower in four of five processes in warm and cold.

The Q-B half of the M=48 change (block_N=128 at block_M=64 for 8192 and 12288) is the real gain. With the weights warm in L2 it is consistent at TP4 (four processes -2.75..-3.44 us on the bench pair, -2.75..-3.62 on the model's pair). At TP3 three of four processes show -6.2..-8.8 us, one shows +2.0, and the cross-image boots read 57.1/57.2 vs 50.3/48.7 us. Cold and NEXT are within the interval.

#1016's 32-row Q-B tiles gained nothing at M=24 beyond the across-process interval in any state. Single processes put the TP3 pair 4.4 us (screen) and 6.3 us (model's pair) slower with the weights in L2.

#1016's 16-row (4096, 1280) block_N=128 tile: in the bench, -1.9..-2.4 us warm at M=1..3 but +2.9 cold / +1.7 NEXT at M=12 (TP4, pooled). In the model it touches only TP8's Q-B: -1.7 us warm at M=1..3, +0.44 +/- 0.12 us warm at M=12, cold within.
NEXT matches cold in this harness (and in h1016): flush, prefetch and join before a single replay leave the pair as slow as a plain flush. The state is measured as the bench defines it.
dropped_from_original: (4096, 1280) block_M=64 threads=64 drop: unstated in #1016. It helps only the bench's indexer kernel, which the model never builds from this table, and it is no faster (slower in 4 of 5 processes) on TP8 Q-B
(4096, 1280) block_M=16 block_N 64->128: slower at M=12 in the bench (epilogue passes) and on TP8 Q-B
(12288|8192, 1280) block_M=32 block_N 64->128: no gain at M=24; TP3 up to +4..6 us in single processes

(16384|6144|2048, 1280) TILE_CONTIGUOUS_FP8 and DECODE_FP8_CONFIGS entries: TP2/TP6/TP7, outside the chained bench. TP6/TP7's trimmed rank unpacks and repacks Q-B, so they need their own change and bench
caveats: The gain is small and confined to M = 33..64 rows with Q-B warm in L2. In cold and NEXT-prefetched L2, closer to serving, r1 is neutral within the interval.
TP3 warm is allocation-sensitive (one process of four disagrees); TP4 is consistent.
One host (sp4). No serving run; the next candidate's qualification decides end to end.
reason: Bit-exact everywhere: outputs hash-equal across images for every pair and M, every arm torch.equal in process, LayerChain digests equal, and pytest passes on both boots. At M = 1..24 r1 compiles 1107's kernels in every pair, so it cannot be slower there. At M = 48, the only changed cell, it gains beyond the interval with the weights warm in L2: TP4 -3.14 +/- 0.30 us paired (x-img -2.89, boot ranges separate) and TP3 -5.14 us paired (x-img -7.70, boot ranges separate; one process of four +2.0). It is within the interval cold and NEXT on both shapes and both indexer builds, and the model's TP8 Q-B is unchanged. No M cell in any L2 state is slower than 1107. The correction drops everything in #1016 that gained nothing, was slower, or fell outside the bench.
